text:
anya: Heads up — we're seeing a rapid spike in KV cache memory across us-west runtime pools and correlated increases in streaming token-latency. Packeted alerts from metrics: mem growth + 4x, token cadence stall up to 12s on tail. Suspect continuous-batching behavior after yesterday's runtime rollout.
ops-bot: Alert -> KV_CACHE_MEM_GROWTH (severity: P2), affected clusters: rw-usw-rt-3/4/5, 2148240000. Peaks at 85% of alloc.
incident-bot: New incident created: INC-2026-214824 (kv-runtime-pulse). Incident commander assigned: @sam_g (oncall).
sam_g: I'm on it. @devon can you pull logs for the runtime worker on rw-usw-rt-4, grep for kv_cache::warmup and batching flush messages? Also list active batching configs.
devon: grabbing logs now. quick snapshot: last deploy 03:10 UTC rolled core/runtime v2.9.3 -> v2.10.0. continuous_batching.enabled=true in that rollout. Logs show recurring "kv_cache:paging:evict" followed by "batching:partial_flush:skipped" roughly every 40-60s.
prod-observability-bot: Top traces for 2148240000: streaming -> long-poll stalls. 37% of traces show >3s token-gap. Related error: "kvcache::page_miss_burst".
luis: Customer-facing note: first signs from two high-QPS customers in us-west experiencing 5-15% increased tail latency on streaming responses. No user data loss reported.
anya: adding context — yesterday's canary used a new eviction bloom filter change + packing for KV pages. Could be interaction with continuous batching that increases per-request KV pressure.
sam_g: mitigation plan: 1) toggle continuous_batching.enabled=false for canary node set in rw-usw-rt-3/4, 2) bump kv_cache.evict_threshold from 0.7 -> 0.85 to delay aggressive paging, 3) enable partial_flush_forced=true to ensure partial batches flush quickly. We'll do in stages and monitor.
devon: patch ready. command to toggle config on the canary pool:
```
rctl config set --cluster rw-usw-rt-3 --service runtime \
  continuous_batching.enabled=false kv_cache.evict_threshold=0.85 \
  batching.partial_flush_forced=true --reason "inc-214824 mitigation"
```
sam_g: run on -3 only first.
devon: applied on rw-usw-rt-3 at 2148240312. rolling to -4 now.
ops-bot: Config change deployed to rw-usw-rt-3 by devon at 2148240312.
prod-observability-bot: Metric update (5m): kv_cache_mem_growth rate down 30% on rw-usw-rt-3; streaming tail p99 token-gap reduced from 11.2s -> 2.9s on that pool.
anya: great signal. roll to -4 once we validate -3 stable for 5m. also want heatmap of batching sizes to confirm partial flush behavior.
devon: rolling to rw-usw-rt-4 at 2148240450. applied exactly same settings.
prod-observability-bot: rw-usw-rt-4 metrics (2m): initial reduction in memory growth, but we see intermittent "kv_cache:eviction-spike" events on node rw-usw-rt-4-07, correlated with "batching:partial_flush:delayed" logs.
sam_g: pause roll to -5. let's not make global change until we understand -4's intermittent spike.
anya: I'm pulling heap profiles from node rw-usw-rt-4-07 and kv cache dump. attaching snippet:
```
kv_cache.entries_by_age: histogram: [0-1s: 120k, 1-10s: 80k, 10-60s: 12k]
pending_batch.queues: avg_size=14, max_size=242
partial_flush_queue: depth spikes at ~180
```
luis: ops note: two paying customers with high concurrency are currently seeing degraded streaming UX (token gaps). CS alerted and asked for ETA.
sam_g: immediate customer mitigation: enable per-tenant KV isolation for the two tenants (throttle their continuous batching) and temporarily route their streaming to non-canary region (us-east) as emergency fallback. @anya can you open route change?
anya: routing change command:
```
rctl route update --tenant customer-alpha,customer-bravo --region us-east --timeout 30s --reason "inc-214824 fallback"
```
anya: route update submitted at 2148240720.
prod-observability-bot: customer-alpha streaming latency normalized after routing -> us-east. customer-bravo still with tail spikes; investigating network hiccup with their origin.
incident-bot: Pager duty escalations: oncall->sre-lead if no resolution in 30m.
sam_g: we need a short-term config that prevents partial flush queues from growing unbounded. Idea: cap pending_batch.max_size=64 and enable batching.prefetch=false for affected pools.
devon: applied cap pending_batch.max_size=64 on rw-usw-rt-4 at 2148241135.
ops-bot: change applied; monitoring.
prod-observability-bot: after cap: partial_flush_queue depth drops 180 -> 22 within 90s, p99 token-gap down to 1.6s on rw-usw-rt-4.
anya: that's promising. but we saw the memory growth earlier; cap helps but root cause likely kv warmup + bloom change + continuous batching prefetch that keeps many pages pinned.
sam_g: next steps: 1) keep cap and per-tenant routing in place, 2) roll back bloom filter change in runtime v2.10.0 if we see reoccurrence after full roll, 3) create postmortem and bug for partial_flush logic (it should honor eviction pressure), 4) notify customers.
luis: I'll draft customer messages: short incident update, impacted customers list, actions taken (routing/fallback, config caps), ETA for next update in 2 hours.
devon: creating rollback PR for bloom filter: PR #5321. If we decide rollback, it needs coordination with infra during low traffic window (approx 22:00 UTC). For now we'll keep mitigations live.
incident-bot: INC-2026-214824 status -> mitigation in progress. commander: @sam_g. severity P2. start_time: 2148240000.
ops-bot: final checks for now: run nightly evict diagnostic after cap; schedule job to collect kv heap dumps every 15m for 3 hours -> uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-214824/
anya: fdn: capture for postmortem: observed interplay: continuous_batching.prefetch + bloom change -> pages pinned -> eviction thrashing -> partial flush queue grows -> token cadence stall. We should add a guard in runtime that pauses prefetch when eviction rate > X.
sam_g: agreed. I'll file two follow-ups: (1) runtime guard PR, (2) improved runbook for streaming stalls including per-tenant routing steps.
luis: customer message posted at 2148241900: "We've routed your traffic and applied mitigations; engineering actively investigating. We'll provide updates every 2 hours." CS confirmed receipt from both customers.
oncall-jen: jumping in for next shift. summary noted. any manual actions I should keep live? current mitigations: cap pending_batch.max_size=64 (rw-usw-rt-4), continuous_batching disabled on rw-usw-rt-3, per-tenant routing for alpha/bravo. Anything else to leave? Also I have PR permissions to run rollback tonight if approved.
sam_g: leave everything as-is. I'll sync with infra for potential rollback window. handoff: oncall-jen you're primary for the next 8h, escalate to me if p99 token-gap > 3s or kv_mem_growth resumes > +20%.
oncall-jen: ack. I'll watch the dashboards and collect the timeline for postmortem. creating the postmortem doc now: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/INC-214824
anya: thanks everyone. keep small updates here. adding remediation tasks to backlog and pinging @research-ml about quantizing prefetch behavior.
prod-observability-bot: Final snapshot at 2148244320: cluster avg token-gap p99 = 1.2s (was 11.2s), kv_cache_mem_growth reduced cluster-wide by ~38% since mitigations. Monitoring until 2148247920.
